messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'redwood/inference-gateway' - INC-20250328-01 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy 'gateway-oncall' triggered, primary oncall jamal_oncall (no ack) -> paging secondary alex
jamal_oncall: seeing it, getting a coffee. on my way to laptop, will ack if it persists
alex: acked. I'm on it — initial check shows 502 spikes from edge to gateway.
maya: tagging in — I can flip the canary routing if this is region-specific.
alex: quick dump of recent errors: ```
ERROR 502 GET /v1/generate  svc-timeout  p50 120ms p95 1.8s p99 6.2s
EDGE -> GATEWAY: 502/timeout from upstream
```
ops-sre: is this a DDOS or upstream capacity? any sudden traffic delta?
alex: traffic looks normal overall, but one AZ in us-west-2 has a burst and gateway pods there are OOM/evicting.
emma_mgr: if primary didn't ack, manager escalation should fire in ~3m. keep us posted, we may need to wake manager if customer impact extends.
maya: rolling a quick route change to avoid the impacted AZ: `kubectl patch svc gateway -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Local"}}'` (will watch)
incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation: manager escalation initiated to emma_mgr (silent)
jamal_oncall: acking now, sorry — DND on mobile hid the page. acked and joining.
alex: no worries — can you join the zoom? I spun up a temporary endpoint routing to green nodes, but about 8% of requests still hit the bad AZ until DNS TTL expires.
jamal_oncall: joining zoom now. thoughts on fallback? we can cut traffic to affected AZ in ELB, but will drop capacity ~20%.
maya: suggestion: failover listeners for the ELB -> remove the AZ from routing: `aws elb deregister-instances-from-load-balancer --instances i-xxxxx` (I can do a controlled drain).
ops-sre: be careful, customers on reserved endpoints might see degraded throughput. Need to communicate to CSM if we degrade below SLA.
emma_mgr: if we expect >10m customer impact, escalate to on-call engineering manager and prepare incident page. what's the current error rate?
alex: error rate peaked at 16% for 2m, now ~6% and falling. median latency back to normal for non-impacted AZs.
maya: started draining the bad AZ pods, traffic rebalanced. putting a conservative autoscaler bump in case of spike.
pagerduty-bot: Secondary oncall alex acknowledged at +120s. Manager emma_mgr notified.
jamal_oncall: re-homed KV cache from the evicted nodes, cache misses dropping. still monitoring.
ops-sre: rolling notice to #customer-impact: "Some customers experienced 502s for ~3 minutes during an AZ eviction, mitigation in progress" — shall I post?
emma_mgr: yes post now, include ETA for full recovery.
ops-sre: posted, included note to CSMs to expect follow-ups.
alex: mitigation seems effective; 502s <1% for last 90s. keep an eye on retry storms.
jamal_oncall: confirming no PagerDuty re-escalation queued.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: no further escalations. Incident status: mitigation in progress.
maya: will leave the drain for 15m then re-evaluate. recommend a follow-up runbook item: investigate pod eviction root cause (kernel OOM vs noisy neighbor) and set pod QoS.
emma_mgr: agreed. schedule a blameless postmortem. alex/jamal/maya, please include timeline and customer-affecting queries. ops-sre, CSM outreach notes.
jamal_oncall: ack, will own the postmortem.
alex: one more ask — add an automated fallback rule to not route new traffic to AZs with >5% 5xx within 60s. we had manual work to do that.
emma_mgr: put a ticket in backlog, mark P1 action item for infra team.
ops-sre: closing the thread in 30m if stable. thanks all. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-20250328-01 acknowledged by jamal_oncall; auto-escalation ended.
incident-bot: Follow-up: create incident entity INC-20250328-01 in ops-issues with severity S2.
jamal_oncall: last check: all healthy. moving to monitoring and postmortem.
alex: resolved for now. will push small QoS change in next deploy window.
emma_mgr: thanks team. debrief tomorrow 11:00.
